parsed_response.reasoning: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: minimumTokenResponseSchema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts only requires access_token; when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set it injects `refresh_token.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when absent, and callers persist the result (GoogleCalendarService writes `key` to prisma.credential.update; Zoom merges `{...credential.key, ...parsedToken.data}`). The sync-mode fetch in refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns only userId/appSlug payload per its comment, so no real refresh token can ever come from that path. Also confirmed: refreshOAuthTokens gates the sync fetch on `userId` being truthy, while parseRefreshTokenResponse's condition omits the userId check, so team-owned credentials (userId null) use the local provider refresh yet get parsed with the permissive sync schema, writing the literal "refresh_token" sentinel over the real token. This permanently corrupts stored credentials — a real data-corruption defect introduced by this diff.

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse injects the literal string "refresh_token" into data.refresh_token whenever the sync-mode schema is selected (a schema that by construction can never produce a real refresh token), and every caller persists that sentinel into credential.key. Zoom (zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts merges {...credential.key, ...parsedToken.data}) and Office365 (CalendarService.ts:263 merge) overwrite the user's real provider refresh_token with the string "refresh_token", and Google stores it wholesale; the moment CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is removed, or for team-owned credentials where userId is null (refreshOAuthTokens takes the local-refresh path at refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 while parsing still uses the sync schema because its condition omits userId), the stored fake token is used against the provider and the credential is permanently bricked — every affected user must re-authenticate every app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` it validates with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, which (by design) does not include `refresh_token`. The function then unconditionally injects `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing. Call sites then persist/merge this into stored credentials, e.g. Office365 (`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` and then updates Prisma, which will overwrite the real `refresh_token` with the sentinel string. Additionally, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`’s condition does not consider `userId`, so even when `refreshOAuthTokens` falls back to the local refresh path for `userId` null (team-owned credentials), parsing can still use the minimum schema and inject the sentinel, causing the stored refresh token to be corrupted as described.
